findings.message: The remount loop does not dispatch layer actions, leaving overlays missing after a basemap switch. When a style switch removes existing overlays, the callback calls layer('disable') and layer('enable') instead of dispatching the atom's action creators. LayerAtom exposes enable/disable actions; the existing applyNewLayerSource implementation uses store.dispatch(layerAtom.disable()) and store.dispatch(layerAtom.enable()) to invoke the renderer lifecycle.

The remount test can pass without any overlay being restored. The test substitutes a bare vi.fn() for the layer atom and only checks that it received 'disable'; it never checks enable, renderer mounting, or the restored map layers. This accepts the incorrect atom calls in the implementation.

Each basemap switch adds another settings subscription that persists until map destruction. The new callback calls layersOrderManager.init on every switch. init pushes a new layersSettingsAtom.subscribe unsubscribe function into _unsubscribe without removing existing subscriptions; cleanup occurs only in destroy.
